# Share an Excerpt

An excerpt lets readers evaluate one or two chapters without receiving the
complete book. It is a separate publication profile built from the same source,
not a manually copied mini-book.

## Select chapters

Edit the `[excerpt]` table in `book.toml`:

```toml
[excerpt]
chapters = ["01-start-here.qmd", "02-write-and-organize.qmd"]
message = "This excerpt contains selected chapters, not the complete book."
```

Choose one or two exact chapter filenames. The introduction, references page,
and necessary presentation files are included automatically; other chapters
and all appendices are excluded.

Write excerpt chapters so they remain understandable without links to omitted
chapters. Keep private material out of shared front and back matter as well as
the selected chapters.

## Build and inspect it

Run:

```sh
make excerpt
```

The command creates HTML, EPUB, and Typst products beneath `_build/excerpt/`.
Inspect all three before sharing them. Confirm that:

- the notice clearly says the publication is incomplete;
- the contents contain only intended chapters;
- links, citations, figures, and references resolve within the excerpt;
- no answer keys, private notes, or unrelated assets are present; and
- title and author metadata are correct.

## Commit source, not products

Commit the manuscript, bibliography, source assets, `book.toml`, Makefile,
README, `.gitignore`, and the managed `.alkahest/scaffold.json` identity record.
Keep `_build/` ignored.

The template creates publication files; it does not decide where you should
upload them. Choose stores, web hosting, identifiers, licenses, companion
hosting, and print vendors near publication, when those decisions are real.
Regular writing is the most valuable workflow test because it reveals where
routine authoring creates friction.
